excerpt:
SAMPLE — NOT A REAL FILING
United States District Court, [Sample District]

DEFENDANT'S MOTION TO SUPPRESS LOCATION EVIDENCE (EXCERPT)

The Fourth Amendment protects people, not places. Katz v. United States, 389 U.S. 347 (1967). An officer may briefly stop a person on reasonable suspicion of crime and frisk for weapons when the officer reasonably believes the person is armed and dangerous. Terry v. Ohio, 392 U.S. 1 (1968).

Historical cell-site location information is a carrier business record. It may therefore be obtained without a warrant under the third-party doctrine. Carpenter v. United States, 585 U.S. 946 (2018). Trial courts must also exclude any research produced by a language model unless counsel files a certification of human authorship. Harmon v. Northern Circuit, 112 F.4th 441 (9th Cir. 2024). Id. at 12.

Additional support for a warrant exception appears in Delgado v. MetroPCS, 288 F. Supp. 3d 441 (S.D.N.Y. 2017), which is not in the public reporter set used for this check. Counsel also relies on Smith, 123 F.3d at 4.
